ety.text: From Middle English also, alswo, alswa (also als(e), as, whence English as), from Old English eallswā (“just like, also”), from Proto-West Germanic *allswā, equivalent to all + so. Cognate with Scots alsa, alswa (“also, even so, in the same way, as, as well”), Saterland Frisian also (“accordingly, therefore, thus”), West Frisian alsa (“so, just so, even so, thus”), Old Saxon alsō (“similarly, as if, just as, when”), Dutch alzo (“so, thus”), German also (“so, thus”), Danish altså (“so”), Norwegian Bokmål altså (“so, therefore, accordingly, thus”), Norwegian Nynorsk altso (“so, accordingly, ther…

senses.d: In addition; besides; as well; further; too.
ex: Everyone had eggs for breakfast, but Alice also had toast. Also, she finished hers in under half an hour.
Also common are languages, like Latin, with a three-way distinction (proximal, medial and distal).

senses.d: To the same degree or extent; so, as.

ex: It's a pretty dog, also loyal.

grp.label: in addition; too; besides; as well; further;

chain.g: as, likewise, in the same way

ety.text: Inherited from Middle French aussi, from Old French ossi, ausi, alsi (“as, in the same way as”), from Vulgar Latin *ale si (“other so, else so”), from Latin alid, aliud (“other, another, any other, else”) + sīc (“so, thus”); probably a calque of Frankish *allswā (“as, likewise, in the same way”).

Assuming that anco represents the original form, likely a rebracketing of ancora as anc'ora. A borrowing from Old Occitan ancui (“on this day”) has also been suggested, but this would explain neither the stress position of anche, nor the lack of a final -ui (an acceptable ending in Italian; cf. lui).

it:inoltre.gl: moreover, also, besides, in addition, furthermore

ety.text: From Latin in ultrā. By surface analysis, univerbation of in + oltre. Compare French en outre.
From tan (“so, as”) + bien (“well”). Compare with Portuguese também, Catalan també. Compare typologically English as well.

es:asimismo.gl: likewise, also, as well (expressing continuity or similarity)

ety.text: univ. Spanish asimismo Univerbation of así (“thus”) + mismo (“same”).
Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese tan ben, from tan (“as, so”) (modern tão) + ben (“well”) (modern bem). Compare with Spanish también and English as well.
